## Addendum — the exact call chain of the FIRST resolution, independently traced

Corroborated by a second, independent read of the same tree (origin/main `6f8a936bb31a`). The
symbolic `--ref` string travels unresolved through six hops before it is rev-parsed for
verification:

1. `_commands/transition_close.py:606-616` — `_completion_precheck(..., ref=ref, ...)`
2. `_commands/close_precheck.py:721-728` — `_verify_with_duration_metrics(..., ref=ref, ...)`
3. `_commands/close_precheck.py:591-599` → `_commands/completion_verifier_run.py:94-100` —
   `close_autoresume.verify_with_auto_resume(..., ref=ref, ...)`
4. `_commands/close_autoresume.py:271-280` — `llm.verify_completion(..., ref=(ref or "HEAD"), fetch=False, source="attested")`
5. `llm/completion.py:332-339` → `llm/gate_source.py:103,116` — `acquire(resolved_ref, ...)`
6. **`_snapshot/cache.py:243` — `sha = resolve_ref(ref, repo_root, fetch=fetch, blobless=False)`**

`verified_at_sha` is then stamped from the handle at `llm/gate_source.py:225-233`
(`result["verified_at_sha"] = handle.sha`). **Nothing threads that resolved sha back into the
close path** — the drift guard only *compares against* it, and re-derives its own via a second
`resolve_ref` at `_commands/transition_close.py:360`. That is the whole defect in one sentence.

A symbolic `--ref` is therefore rev-parsed **twice** per close on the legacy tail (three times if
the op-cert reuse fast path runs — `_commands/close_autoresume.py` `target_sha = resolve_ref(ref or "HEAD", root, fetch=False)`;
that one fails closed to a fresh verify, so it is not itself harmful).

### `fetch=False` semantics — why `origin/main` is STRICTLY WORSE than `HEAD`

`_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:247-298`: with `fetch=False`, `remote_present` is unconditionally
False (`:265`), both fetch branches are skipped (`:269`, `:282`), and the only work done is
`rev_parse(root, ref)` (`:281`) — `git rev-parse --verify --quiet --end-of-options <ref>^{commit}`
(`_snapshot/git_fetch.py:181-192`). Nothing caches the value; each call shells out afresh against
the on-disk ref store.

So `refs/remotes/origin/main` is mutable local state that ANY process sharing the `.git` can
advance — a concurrent `git fetch`/`pull`/`remote update`, including from another worktree, since
remote-tracking refs live in the SHARED common dir. `HEAD` (the case 4de6 fixed) moves only when
someone commits in this worktree; `origin/main` moves whenever anyone anywhere fetches. The
unfixed half of the invariant is the more exposed half.

### One more independent HEAD read, noted but not causal

`_engine_support/commit_impact.py:193-197` — the landing check's `git log` runs with **no rev
argument**, i.e. it walks the current HEAD regardless of `--ref`. That is documented behaviour
(AGENTS.md: `--ref` "does not narrow the referencing-commit scan") and it feeds reachability, not
the drift comparison — so it is not part of this mechanism. Recorded so a later reader does not
re-derive it.

### What a fix would and would not break (test impact, pre-computed)

No test asserts the NUMBER of `resolve_ref` calls, and no test passes a symbolic ref through a
close. Extending the pin at `transition_close.py:575-589` to the `ref is not None` case leaves the
existing suite intact: `test_close_ref_target_80af.py:87` already passes a concrete sha (which
resolves to itself) and `:111` already expects a resolved sha. Only tests pinning the drift
OUTCOME would need review, and only if the fix changed drift semantics rather than removing the
spurious trigger — it does the latter:
`tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_attested_signing.py:239-263`
(`test_presign_sha_drift_closes_without_signature_and_warns`, which pins close-exit-0 +
`unsigned` + the stderr text) and `tests/unit/test_transition_close.py:186-192`
(pins `cause == "material_drifted"`). Both use synthetic non-matching SHAs, so both keep passing.
